From the above equation, the Charles's law can be defined as, the ratio
between volume and the absolute temperature of the given mass of a gas is
constant at constant pressure.
Experimental Verification of Charles's law
The apparatus used for the experimental verification of the Charles's law
consists of a cylinder. The cylinder has a piston. The walls of the cylinder are
heat insulator while the base of the cylinder is heat conductor. When the
cylinder is heated at constant pressure, the piston move upward and the
volume will increase. It is noted from various observations that the ratio
between volume and absolute temperature remains constant. This verifies
Charles's law.
